It takes you a moment to notice his sobbing over the noise of the waves. "I've got to tell them, haven't I? I'll go to the port in the morning and see if they'll take me." You can no longer make him out in the dark, but his hand touches your shoulder as he leaves.

He doesn't reply. After a minute, you feel along the sand in the dark towards where he sat. Your hand closes on a discarded shirt. The rest of his clothes make a path to the edge of the water. You can't follow him any further.
ru: Вы наслаждаетесь отдыхом на пляже, лежа на самом краю мира, но солнце уже начинает садиться, а ветер усиливается. Вы уже собираетесь подняться, когда рядом плюхается какой-то человек. Он садится на почтительном расстоянии, но выжидающе поглядывает на вас.

Он вяло улыбается: «Меня только что уволили». «Первое испаноамериканское радио в штате, а они меня вышвыривают. Понимаю, кого-то сократить было необходимо, но я же в два раза... — он останавливается. — Даже не знаю, как об этом сказать жене».

«Меня только что уволили», — прорывает его. «Первое испаноамериканское радио в штате, а они меня вышвыривают. Понимаю, кого-то сократить было необходимо, но я же в два раза... — он останавливается. — Даже не знаю, как об этом сказать жене».

«Попробую попытать удачи в доках, но там и так людей больше, чем работы, да и платят столько, что семью сложно прокормить, — он опускает голову. — А мой мальчик... просто не знаю, как им сказать. Я не знаю, что делать».

Он успокаивается, глядя как солнце опускается за горизонт. Над вами простирается темное небо. Только зажегшиеся в городе фонари напоминают, что мир не исчез полностью. Выдержав долгую паузу, мужчина заговаривает: «Жизнь уже никогда не наладится?»

Спустя мгновение вам удается расслышать за плеском волн его всхлипывания: «Рассказать все же придется, верно? А с утра отправлюсь в порт и постараюсь устроиться». Вы уже совершенно не видите его в темноте, но ощущаете, как он касается вашего плеча, перед тем как уйти.

Он не отвечает. Спустя минуту вы слышите удаляющийся скрип песка. Ваша рука нащупывает сброшенную рубашку. Остальная его одежда также валяется на земле, образуя дорожку к воде. Дальше вы за ним последовать не можете.

stories.title: Mill
en: The man is the color of mill dust. His smile creases his face like folds in dough. He gestures you inside the dilapidated structure and shouts over the sound of driving wheels: "You're welcome to sleep here. You don't want to rest by the river, not in the evening. Insects."

The man shoves the broken door closed behind you. The mill is warm and the air is heavy with the powder kicked up by your entrance. You realize how easy it would be to drift off on this pile of sacks, to the loud but constant sound of the grinding wheels...

Pain sears your spine. Why did you sleep at this ridiculous angle? Your back complains from being draped over... the millstone? It's good the mill is totally abandoned, its works long ago disconnected—or your legs would've been pulverized. The man is gone... hmm. This is not a place to linger.

Consciousness is elusive—your limbs throb with a dull fatigue and your eyes are sticky with dust. The man suddenly grips your legs and drags you towards the millstone. "You do not love my daughter. You will not have her. I will not let you hurt her." His voice is pained, not angry.

Your hand catches a flour sack printed with brightly colored flowers. A puff of flour makes you sneeze—and you wake. The mill is quiet; its works long disconnected. In your hand is the faded remnant of what might once have been a bag, or a piece of dress.
ru: Мужчина вымазан в муке с головы до ног. Улыбка его кажется складкой на тесте. Он жестом приглашает вас в обветшалое строение и кричит так, чтобы было слышно за грохотом жерновов: «Можешь отоспаться здесь. У реки на ночь лучше не останавливаться. Насекомые сожрут».

Мужчина затворяет за вами перекошенную дверь. Внутри мельницы тепло, а стоит вам войти, в воздух вздымается густое облако мучной пыли. Вы понимаете, как сладко будет прикорнуть на груде мешков под пусть и громкий, но монотонный скрип жерновов...

Вашу спину пронзает боль. Почему вы спите в столь странной позе? Позвоночник болит, потому что вы... свисаете с колеса жернова? Хорошо, что мельница абсолютно пуста и бездействует... иначе ваши ноги уже бы перемололо. А тот мужчина исчез... Хм-м. Не стоит здесь задерживаться.

Ваше сознание уплывает... конечности наливаются усталостью, а глаза залепляет мука. Мужчина неожиданно хватает вас за ноги и тащит к жерновам: «Ты не любишь мою дочь. И ее не получишь. Я не позволю ей навредить». В его голосе звучит мука, а не гнев.

Ваша рука натыкается на мешок муки, на котором напечатаны яркие цветы. Взметнувшееся облачко пыли заставляет вас чихнуть... и вы просыпаетесь. На мельнице тихо; она уже давно бездействует. Ваша рука сжимает выцветшую ткань, которая когда-то могла быть или клочком мешка, или лоскутом платья.

stories.title: Minneapolis Strike
en: Three delivery trucks sit on the waterfront, their drivers securing the cargo. Twelve cop cars form a protective half-ring around them. Their occupants seem to be gearing up for combat.

You approach a pair of cops. The broad one pushes shells into a shotgun with a practiced motion and an undercurrent of excitement. His wiry partner indicates the trucks. "We've got to get these through, keep 'em secure."
The broad cop grunts. "You been livin' under a rock?" "Strikers," says the other. "Socialist motherfuckers," the broad one adds. The wiry cop looks away.

The broad cop sneers. "Does it matter? They'd better fall in line." The other shakes his head. "My cousin's out there, I don't think their demands are—" "Maybe you're standing on the wrong side. Come on." They walk off to join a briefing huddle.

It's a token act of resistance, but it's something. You drop onto your belly, the car between you and the gathered cops, and locate the fuel line. You jab a knife into it. It takes a few attempts, but you nick it just right, and cover your face as gasoline flows out.
You stand to find the thin cop watching. He looks between you and the fuel leaking over the asphalt. The two of you lock eyes for a long second. "Go," he says.
Whatever your feelings, there's nothing you can do. You turn away and walk back towards the river.
ru: У воды стоят три грузовика, чье содержимое охраняют их водители. Вокруг них полукольцом выстроилось двенадцать машин полиции. Их пассажиры, похоже, готовятся к сражению.
Вы подходите к двум копам. Широкоплечий отточенными движениями и с явным наслаждением заряжает дробовик. Его тощий напарник кивает на грузовики: «Мы с этим покончим. Нельзя их упустить».
Широкоплечий коп усмехается: «Ты в пещере, что ли, живешь?» — «Стачечники», — говорит второй. — «Социалистическое отребье», — добавляет первый. Тощий полицейский отводит взгляд.

Широкоплечий коп усмехается: «Какая разница? Им стоит перестать бунтовать». Второй качает головой: «У меня там родственник, и я не думаю, что их требования...» — «А может, ты просто не на той стороне? Идем». Они направляются к совещающемуся отряду.

Пусть это и слабый акт неповиновения, но хотя бы что-то. Вы падаете на живот, заползаете под машину полицейских и находите бензопровод. А затем втыкаете в него нож. Удается справиться не сразу, но наконец получается, и на лицо вам льется бензин.
Поднявшись, вы понимаете, что на вас смотрит тощий коп. Он видит и вас, и то, как топливо разливается по асфальту. Ваши глаза встречаются всего на секунду. «Уходи», — произносит он.
Какие бы чувства вы ни испытывали, а поделать ничего нельзя. Вы разворачиваетесь и уходите к реке.

stories.title: Miracle Growth
en: The plants grow and blossom as you watch. The man goes down the line, applying a few drops from a vial as he goes. As the liquid soaks in, each plant pushes up from the soil, unfolding and stretching for the sky.

He turns to you. "Quite something, isn't it? The soil here strangles the crops, and people are starving. Even when the plants survive, they don't grow fast enough to fill people's bellies." He smiles. "My miracle formula will change that."
He shakes his head. "I'm not giving up my secrets that easily. The state will pay a lot of money for this." He shakes the vial. He tears off a leaf. "Here, try some."

It's just bitter at first, but as you swallow, the fibrous mass burns in your throat. You fight to hold it down, and your stomach knots tight when the plant matter hits it. You cough and hiccup. The man looks at you, curious. "What do you think?"

He waves a hand. "Well, yes, there are some kinks to work out, but people are starving! They can't be fussy. It won't be long before no one round here goes hungry again!" Your stomach protests. You feel like you'll be hungry again very soon indeed.

He beams. "Fantastic! Tell you the truth, the last few batches haven't worked out quite right, but clearly I'm making progress. It won't be long before no one round here goes hungry again!" Your stomach protests. You feel like you'll be hungry again very soon indeed.
ru: Посадки вырастают и расцветают прямо у вас на глазах. Мужчина идет вдоль полосы, капая на каждую из своего флакона. Как только жидкость попадает на растение, оно тут же вырывается из земли, распускается и тянется к небу.

Он поворачивается к вам: «Удивительно, правда? Почвы здесь неплодородны, и люди голодают». «Даже если посадки выживают, они растут слишком медленно, чтобы насытить животы, — он улыбается. — — Мой чудесный эликсир это исправит».
Он качает головой: «Так просто я своих тайн не выдаю. Власти штата отвалят мне за это кучу деньжат». Он потряхивает флаконом. А затем срывает листок: «Вот, попробуй».

Вначале вы чувствуете лишь горечь, но, когда проглатываете волокнистую массу, горло начинает жечь. Подступает рвота, а желудок просто скручивает, когда съеденное проваливается в него. Вы начинаете кашлять и икать. Мужчина с интересом наблюдает за вами: «Ну и как тебе?»

Он взмахивает рукой: «Ну да, кое над чем еще надо поработать, но люди-то голодают! Не время привередничать. Совсем скоро никто в этих краях не будет знать недостатка в еде!» Ваш желудок протестует. И у вас такое чувство, что совсем скоро вы снова будете голодны.

Он аж лучится: «Чудесно! Если честно, последние пробы были не слишком удачными, но я явно иду в верном направлении. Совсем скоро никто в этих краях не будет знать недостатка в еде!» Ваш желудок протестует. И у вас такое чувство, что совсем скоро вы снова будете голодны.

stories.title: Molasses Man
en: He sings as he works, his voice warm and soft as the late afternoon sun. The air's sweet with the tang of recently-cut sugar cane. There's a practiced, almost soothing precision to the way he works. He looks up and nods hello.
"Making molasses," he says to your unasked question. "I sell the blackstrap in town. Farmers use it for feed. Bitter as hell." He grins.

"Got some set aside." He comes back with a murky flask, waving off any offer of payment. "I ain't chargin'. Folk round here need what they can get. Makes a mean loaf of bread." He nods at the barrels. "I'm about done filtering. Got to boil it next. Lend a hand?"

"I don't notice it no more—been doing this a while. I keep back a few bottles to share. I don't charge, neither. Folk round here need what they can get. Makes a mean loaf of bread." He nods at the barrels. "I'm about done filtering. Got to boil it next. Lend a hand?"

You help him haul the barrels over to the metal boiler. You pour in the juice and set the fire. It's hot work. He fetches water and dark bread, and you share the small meal and a smile. "It's good to find another who takes joy in honest labor."

"I guess not everyone finds joy in labor." He offers a few coins. You help him haul the barrels over to the metal boiler. You pour in the juice and set the fire. It's hot work. He fetches water and dark bread, and you share the small meal.
ru: Он напевает за работой; голос у него мягкий и теплый, точно полуденное солнце. В воздухе витает аромат свежесрезанного сахарного тростника. Движения человека отточены и плавны. Он оглядывается и здоровается с вами кивком.
«Готовлю патоку, — отвечает он на ваш немой вопрос. — Для рома, который потом в городе продаю. Фермеры хлещут его как воду. Хотя он адски ядреный». Он усмехается.

«У меня еще немного осталось, — он возвращается с бутылью мутного пойла и отмахивается от оплаты. — Это подарок. Люди сейчас нуждаются в утешении. Считай, что мы разделили с тобой хлеб». Он кивает на бочки: «Фильтрация почти закончилась. Пора приступать к варке. Поможешь?»

«Я уже привык... и поступаю так довольно давно — держу пару бутылок в запасе. И денег за них не беру. Люди сейчас нуждаются в утешении. Считай, что мы разделили с тобой хлеб». Он кивает на бочки: «Фильтрация почти закончилась. Пора приступать к варке. Поможешь?»

Вы помогаете ему перелить сок из бочек в металлический чан. А закончив, разводите огонь. Не самая простая работа. Мужчина наливает воды и режет хлеб. Вы перекусываете и улыбаетесь друг другу: «Приятно встретить того, кто любит честный труд».

«Похоже, не все находят радость в труде», — он предлагает несколько монет. Вы помогаете ему перелить сок из бочек в металлический чан. А закончив, разводите огонь. Не самая простая работа. Мужчина наливает воды и режет хлеб. Вы перекусываете.

stories.title: Money Major City
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

You're standing outside a department store that emphatically had no day work available, when an exasperated woman carrying a small terrier rushes out onto the sidewalk. "Here, you!" she says. "Won't you watch him for me? He keeps chewing the shoes, and I'll only be a minute."
"Thank you!" she cries and heads inside again. The terrier seems perfectly content in your arms until she returns and scoops him up, leaving you with a very generous tip.
"Well!" she snaps, and hurries down the street in a huff.
You sit outside a grocery store with your hat out until a young man in an apron quietly asks you to leave. "My mom says she's gonna come out and kick your ass," he whispers.
"Please," the kid whispers. He digs around in his pocket and comes up with a couple coins. He throws them down in your hat and again begs you to go: "Please! She's not joking!"
The kid hurries back inside. You lounge outside and watch folks go by; a few more coins land in your hat. The sun's warm, people are friendly… this is almost relaxing!

You wake very suddenly when that ass-kicking mom flings you over the nearest hedge. "GET OUT," she bellows. Your hat and your coins follow, scattering in the grass. The towering, blood-smeared butcher who threw them stomps back into the store.
No one gives you anything, but to be fair, no one seems to have much to give. This is a broken town in a broken country.

You pack your stuff and hurry down the street. When you glance over your shoulder, you see a towering woman in a blood-stained butcher's apron watching you from the door to the grocery. Her crossed arms bulge with muscle like—like a pair of crossed seals. Wow.

stories.title: Money Major City10
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.
A tiny woman in a lush fur coat is standing outside a boutique lamp store with package nearly as tall as she is. "You there," she calls. "Can you lift this?"

It's huge and unwieldy, but light as anything. "Carry it down to my house and we'll work something out," the woman declares. You heft the package and follow her. She begins a rambling story about her living room, her interior decorator, her husband's taste in rugs…
You can't see her over the top of the box, so you tune her voice out and start thinking about other things. Suddenly, though, you realize you've lost track of her voice entirely!

She must have taken a turn you didn't notice. You're in the middle of a residential street with an enormous box labelled FRAGILE. THIS SIDE UP. LAMP. You are not dressed like a lamp owner. People are watching you from their windows. Time to make yourself scarce.
You follow by the sound of her voice: the lamp box is so large you can't see a thing. Eventually she exclaims: "Here we are!"

You lay the box down in her living room. It's nowhere near as luxurious as she made it sound: a card table, a ratty couch, and a wall tapestry done in a grotesque imitation medieval style. "This will really tie the room together," she exclaims. At least she tips you!

For most of the day, people are particularly stingy. It's probably because there's a puppeteer up the road who's making a little man play a guitar and doing the noises with his mouth. His hat is overflowing with coins. Goddamn him! Attention hog!

You're about to leave when you see the puppeteer packing up his stuff—thank God! You're surprised, however, when he starts walking in your direction. He tips a good third of the money from his hat into yours. "Sorry about that," he says, sheepishly. "I know how it is."

"You ever think of acquiring a gimmick?" he asks. "I slept rough for five years before I learned this puppet crap. I got a friend who took up ventriloquism." He shrugs. "People like to feel as if they're rewarding hard work. It's bullshit, though. Puppets ain't good for anything."
Nope. Nothing. Goddamn it! Nobody will even look you in the eye. This whole city sucks.

stories.title: Money Major City11
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

It starts to rain in the kind of torrential, tree-stripping way that only happens once or twice a year. Everyone scrambles for cover. But one guy stays out in the street: a fellow with a bale of bent and lopsided umbrellas. "TEN CENTS EACH," he hollers.

The rain has soaked him through, but he's doing a roaring trade. "Hey," he tells you. "Go run around on the main shopping streets and pick up all the umbrellas you see, ok? People sometimes drop'em when they blow inside-out. I'll pay!"

He's liable to get pneumonia out there! You take shelter in a restaurant packed with damp, smelly, rained-on folks. The freak thunderstorm is over in an hour. You wonder if the umbrella-seller managed to make any profit.

He's right: there are umbrellas scattered all up and down the street like fallen birds. You gather up an armful, and the umbrella-seller buys 'em all off you for a couple coins. The next morning, though, your throat is hoarse and your nose is running like a faucet. Damn it!

It starts to rain after only a few hours. You shuffle your setup backward into the shelter of a store awning, but the shop-owner keeps threatening to call the cops, and nobody's out here paying beggars in the rain, anyway. Goddamn it!

You pick your stuff up and start looking for a new doorway. But everywhere you go, everyone threatens to call the cops! What is it with this city and cops? When the rain finally stops, you open up your knapsack and discover you've been carrying around a gallon of rainwater. Shit.
Soon, the shopowner does call the cops on you. There's two. The big one cracks his knuckles. "Make yourself scarce," he commands, tossing your bag out into the rain. Shit!

You grab your stuff and scurry down the road. The rain gets into everything. Your coat soaks through almost immediately. When the rain finally stops, you open up your knapsack and discover you've been carrying around a gallon of water. Damn.

The other cop seems to agree that this was too much. "Hey, hey," he tells his partner, pulling your bag out of a puddle. "Cool off." He returns your bag—with a few coins hidden in his palm. "You don't have to go home, but you can't stay here," he says. The other cop spits.
Nobody gives you a cent, the street is relentlessly smelly, and you feel like garbage. Ugh. Time to get going.

stories.title: Money Major City12
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

The factory gates swing open. "Who here can use a sewing machine?" shouts the foreman. You can mend holes with a needle and thread, but you haven't lived in the same house as a sewing machine in years…

You don't much like the idea of walking through those heavy doors, into the power of those cruel-eyed folks, under the burden of a lie. You stay silent. They take in a few more workers for hauling and lifting, but that's the end of it. No work today.
You're ushered into a factory filled with machines you've never seen before. You see spools of leather straps, sliding frames of steel… nothing you recognize.

They explain the machinery to your group, but the instructions are totally mystifying. A thick-armed woman next to you makes a grunt of recognition. She probably actually knows how to use a sewing machine, huh? You know you absolutely cannot fake competency here.

You let your legs go loose and fall flat onto your ass, dropping your stuff everywhere. The workers in the crowd yelp and back away; the foreman crouches over you in a panic. He slaps you once across the face. "Hey! Hey!! Oh, shit, oh, shit…"

Much to your surprise, they're incredibly kind about it. They carry you into a side room and leave you on a cot. You lie there for hours until you're sure they buy it. You get no pay, of course, but they let you go without a fuss, urging you to take it easy.

The foreman breaks into uproarious laughter. "I get at least one of you folks a day," he says. "Everyone wants work. Look, I appreciate your coming clean." He turns to the rest of the group. "ANYONE ELSE WANNA ADMIT THEY CAN'T SEW?" No one raises their hand.

The foreman makes a counter-offer: heavy lifting in the back warehouse. Pays less than working with the machines, but hey, it's money! All day long, though, whenever you see the foreman walking by, you feel a flush of embarrassment break out on your cheeks.

You sit down across the street from a Catholic church. The bulky building behind it looks like a school, but the kids don't congregate on this street, so no one comes to chase you away from them. You get a couple coins before lunch, but it gets slow in the middle of the day.

At noon, you the bell rings up in the church steeple, followed shortly by the school-bell echoing through the maze of outbuildings. A minute later, a door pops open and a nun starts crossing the street toward you with a tray in her hand.

Smiling broadly, she says something kindly in a language you don't recognize and lays the tray on the street. It's school food… bad school food. Damp sandwich with a single slice of cheese, withered apple, bowl of greyish chicken soup. The glass of apple juice seems good as any, though.
You try to demur. She doesn't understand. You push the tray away with a finger and nod and apologize. She pushes the tray back, worry creeping across her face.

You turn your head away and stare into the middle distance, lips clamped shut. The nun shuffles over to enter your gaze; you turn your head the other way. This goes back and forth for a few minutes until she turns and runs back into the church.

Moments later, another nun pops out. "YOU WANT FOOD OR NOT?" she shouts. No thanks, you say. "Well, okay, I guess," the nun calls back. She goes inside; you don't see a single additional nun for the rest of the day. (No one comes to collect the tray, either.)

"Thanks but no thanks," you announce, over and over again. "Thanks but no thanks!!" Suddenly, the nun turns on her heel and runs back into the church. Moments later, another nun pops out. "YOU WANT THIS FOOD OR NOT?" she shouts across the road.

"Well, okay, I guess," the nun shouts back. She goes inside; you don't see a single additional nun for the rest of the day. No one comes to collect the food, either. (Eventually, you just set it on a nearby windowsill.)

You start shoveling the food down. It's… bad. The sandwich cheese is revoltingly slimy, and the chicken soup is so salty your tongue feels like an assassinated snail. The nun is grinning at you, commenting now and again in that language you don't recognize.

You offer the tray back. Before she takes it, the nun lays a hand on your shoulder. "God bless you," she pronounces, and her thick, buttery accent makes her sound like she might really be speaking for him. Despite the foul meal, you feel strangely renewed.
Not a single cent all day. No one will even look at you. You're not sure whether they're embarrassed they have so little charity, or embarrassed they have nothing to be charitable with.

stories.title: Money Major City13
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

This hospital needs someone to mop floors for the day. A nurse gives you instructions, rat-tat-tat: scrub Surgery A and Floor 2, skip the rooms with the newborns, ask Doctor Penny if he wants his office done, this is very important, get these hallways before lunch…
You try to remember all the nurse's very important instructions, but it's impossible. You haven't seen her in hours, this place is busy as hell, and nobody's watching you…

You mop random rooms and hallways as fast as you can, totally at random. Around lunch, someone in a suit waves you down and hands you a plate of lunch; at about three, a nurse gives you an ice cream cone. Sick kids wave at you. A doctor(??) shakes your hand!

When the nurse tracks you down at the end of the day, she's beaming. "You did a wonderful job!" She fills your hand with cash. "Everyone was so impressed! This place has never been so clean!" You keep your secret method to yourself.

You roll your bucket through the halls, asking other folks where she might be, but it turns out that "dark-haired middle-aged woman in nurse clothes" describes about fifty people in this building. Eventually, you find her in a room with a wheezing child.

Brow furrowed, she opens her mouth to admonish you… then stops. "Well, actually I don't remember," she admits. "Just mop stuff, okay?" You spend the rest of the day absently mopping stuff; the pay is just okay.

You find an excellent spot outside a grocer; for hours, people come out and hand you their change. Excellent! Soon you're absolutely flush with cash. When lunch comes around, you think you can afford to buy a healthy, bracing meal for yourself.
You pocket the money. Who knows what trouble you'll have to buy off down the road?

You head into the grocer and purchase a loaf of bread, a chunk of cheese, a whole tomato, a bottle of mustard, some slices of turkey, and a head of lettuce. You create four sandwiches and eat them all. Delicious! You feel like you could walk a hundred miles without stopping!
Sour cloudy skies, and sour faces on the passerby. The folks here are distant; you end up with nothing more than a sore ass.

stories.title: Money Major City14
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.
Doors close in your face one by one, like giant dominos: boom, boom, boom. Bad luck today, or is it something else?

You don't have much to change your outfit with, but you rearrange your various layers and tip your hat at a spunky angle. And the next place—boom. Yikes. That one was even more emphatic than the others.
Hello, friend! I'm up for anything, super flexible, a real self-starter, my, this place looks nice—boom. Yikes. That one was even more emphatic than the others.

A pair of elderly folks are sitting on a park bench near your spot. The old man is watching you carefully; you hope there won't be be any trouble. Your worst fears are confirmed when he stands and starts hobbling toward you…

To your surprise, the old man gives you a shiny, fat coin. "My wife doesn't know it," he whispers, "but when she met me, I was a wanderer too." He gives you a wink. "I told her my sister and I were students new in town, but we didn't have a home, and we were wild as anything!"

The wife in question is obliviously reading a book. "There ain't no rules in life," the old man says. "Ain't nobody only one thing. You can wander for awhile and turn right around and work in a school, or a lawyer office, or whatever you like." He pats you on the shoulder. "Be free first, I say."
No luck today. Maybe your spot was bad; maybe people are avoiding you. Precious few pass you by, fewer make eye contact, and none of them pass you a coin.

stories.title: Money Major City2
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

Shouts echo from a nearby alley. You discover a crowd of men unloading sacks from a truck as fast as they can. When the truck empties, it roars away, and another surges up to take its place. The sacks are lumpen, heavy, and stained with dark smears.

"Yes," blurts a laborer. "Do we ever!" An older fellow, however, throws out his arm to shut the man up. "Uh, we don't need help with the stuff," he says, stepping close—to obscure your view of the goods. "Mind fetching water instead?" He waggles a few coins in your direction.

You fill their pail at a nearby gas station. When you return, though, the men are waiting in the alley innocent as anything. They wash a sticky residue off their hands in the water, and their boss passes you a couple coins. There's no sign of the goods anywhere.
"Suit yourself," he snorts. "And clear outta here, okay? This is private property." Behind him, men fling sacks into an open garage. None of them will make eye contact with you.
A man in a nice suit, looking very pensive, strolls up and sits on the curb beside you.

He nods distractedly. "You know, I've been working since I was a little fella," he begins. "I worked my way up and I built my company from nothing." He hasn't even looked at you; he doesn't need a response. "Now it's back to nothing, again," he sighs.

He looks at you for the first time. "Here," he says suddenly, pulling a well-worn bill from his pocket. "It was my first, and now it's my last. I don't really need it any more." He hands you the money, and with a jaunty spring in his step, strolls towards the nearby railway underpass.
After a while he gets up again and walks away slowly towards the nearby railway underpass, fingering something in his pocket.
Nobody tosses you a coin today, but honestly, they don't look like they have much to give. Everyone in the street seems tired. Even the dogs are walking with a droop. Time to move on, perhaps.

stories.title: Money Major City3
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

You wait outside a lumber warehouse for hours. You don't get there early enough for work in the warehouse, but trucks swing by every few minutes, picking up loads of fresh wood—and sometimes a few people from the street-corner for a job elsewhere in the city.

A battered pickup stops at the curb. There's only a few planks in the bed of the truck, and the cab is packed with teenagers. A young man with a bent cigarette drooping from his lip shouts to you: "HEY! WANNA MAKE SOME CASH?"
"Suckin' my diiiii—" "Shut UP," blurts the smoker, shoving his companion hard. "It's, it's painting—painting a house," he says.

You sit against the wall of an apartment building and put your hat on the sidewalk. Only a couple minutes later, however, a flowerpot glances painfully off your arm and shatters on the ground beside you. Passerby gasp and scatter.

"GET THE FUCK OUTTA HERE, BUM," someone shouts from a second-story window. You scramble under an awning for protection—just in time. The flowerpot's drip tray shatters on the sidewalk exactly where you were sitting. "Stop that," screams a woman with a stroller.
Your shoulder aches like hell. Luckily, your assailant's attention has been diverted into a screaming argument with the mother—and three other people in the street. No one notices you leave.
A good haul today! These people are unusually generous. Your hat is heavy with coins, and your heart is a little lighter than it was this morning.

The boys in the truck start screaming a lot of really vile stuff. The driver, red-faced, stomps on the gas so hard that the flap on the back of the truck flops open and his two-by-fours scatter all over the street. Dodged a bullet there, probably.

The door of the truck cab opens slowly, and the boys slide around to make room for you. You count them quick: six total, two of them crouched under the dashboard at the foot of the front passenger seat. There's something ominous about their sudden silence.

The moment the truck pulls into the street, every single boy but the driver produces a switchblade of some sort. Everything is bare knees and shining knifeblades. "GIVE US YOUR MONEY," howls the driver, accelerating into the middle lane.

You reach back for the door latch—and a second later you're landing hard in the middle of the street. The truck roars away, the boys' shocked faces craned back to look at you. A taxi nearly runs you over; passerby jeer as you limp to the curb. It could have been worse.

stories.title: Money Major City4
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

Diggin' holes. Not what you had in mind, but damn, they're diggin' a lot of holes in this park! A foreman assigns you to a workgroup with a mix of other dishevelled men and women and sends you off to dig a pit by the water fountain.

Nobody wants to say. A young woman keeps mouthing something to you across the hole, but you can't make it out. What is she saying? Dear lobby? Dave hobby? Dean bobber? You never get anyone to admit what this is all about, but you do get paid pretty ok.

The foreman keeps coming by to ask what you've found. At one point, you dig up something suspiciously bone-like, and everyone gets really excited. It breaks apart in the foreman's hands, though: just a rotten stick.
By nightfall, your many holes have turned up nothing interesting. The foreman pays out pretty well, though.
You set yourself up under a statue of a man on a horse and lay your hat out on the ground. A few minutes later, you notice a very small child eyeing you from across the plaza.
He returns a nervous smile. A few moments later, you see him walk over to a bench and whisper something in his mother's ear.
His eyes remained glued on you with an expression you can't quite read. A few minutes later, you see him walk over to a bench and whisper something in his mother's ear.
No charity from this city today. Maybe they're all broke. You'd believe it, too—you haven't seen anyone in hours who looks like they know where their next dinner's coming from.
The child takes something from her and crosses the plaza. He drops some coins right into your hat and gives you a solemn nod. "God bless you," he whispers.

stories.title: Money Major City5
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

Miraculously, you're one of the first people in line when this factory's doors open! You join a crowd of people streaming through the machine-room toward the back. When the doors to the furthest storage-room open, though, the folks in the front ranks recoil. A few even scream!
"YOU WANNA GET PAID, DONCHA?" shouts the foreman. "GET IN THERE! GET IN!" The folks behind you shove forward, and soon you're pushed inside. Holy shit: this room is full of fucking snakes!!

"Grab 'em!" shouts the foreman, passing out nets. "They're haaaaarmless!" The remaining workers get over their fear and start scooping up snakes by the netful. The beasts hiss pathetically; you dump them into a chute in the far wall.

It does pay pretty well. During lunch, you rest on the warehouse floor; the snakes pile up in a corner and watch you all with enormous suspicion. It's then that you glance out a window and notice a fading logo on a sign outside: SYLVESTER BROS. FINE BOOTS. Poor snakes!

You join the majority of workers in a headlong dash back out of the factory. The men at the front gate let a new worker in for every one that flees, but the crowd is beginning to disperse. (Someone musta told them a little more about the job.)

You're sitting across the street from a busy restaurant with a little sign on a plank of wood: HELP ME BUY FOOD! Most of the passerby give you nasty looks. There's a lady in the front window of the restaurant who can't stop staring, either.

Just as you're about to give up, however, you see some motion inside the restaurant. The lady's paid her check, and now she's bustling to the door. To your surprise, she makes a beeline across the street—right for you!

You can't tell if she's excited to help you, or pissed that you're here, but she slaps a pile of coins into your hat and starts machine-gunning you with questions. "What's your name? Who's your mother? Why are you dressed like this? Why are you here?"

She glares at you like a hawk glares at a rat caught in its talons. "You look exactly like someone I know," she growls, maintaining eye-contact for much too long. "EXACTLY!" And with that, she turns on her heel and stomps away. Strange! Generous, at least—but very strange!
No luck today. After hours of roasting in the sun, your hat is still empty. You're not sure it's down to unfriendliness, though—everyone here is just as dusty and hungry and shabby as you.

stories.title: Money Major City6
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

You join a crew of laborers waiting at a street-corner. Soon, a truck pulls up, and everyone jumps in the back. "The job's good," one woman assures you. You ride a short way before the truck pulls up behind a factory. Everyone hops out—and starts putting on heavy coats!
The whole factory is a vast, cold meat-locker. You're shivering in only a few minutes. Dragging the carcasses around is hard work, but it only keeps you so warm; soon, your hands are totally numb.
You grit your teeth and keep working. By nightfall, you're shaking almost uncontrollably. You're paid a full day's wages, but it's hardly worth it.
"Next time, bring the right clothes," grumbles the foreman. He gives you a half-day's wages.

You're having a hard time finding a place to set up that's close enough to foot-traffic, but far enough from the main strip of bars to keep the drunks away. You see a promising doorway—but someone else is hunkered down there already.
The other beggar sees you pacing in frustration and waves you over. "I'm about to clear out," she says. "Swap with me. This spot is really good." She gives you a kindly wink.
And she's right: you take in an excellent haul in only a couple hours. Enough for a several hot meals, maybe!
No luck. Everyone here's a tight-assed snob. Time to go, probably.

stories.title: Money Major City7
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.
You're waiting for the light to change outside a corner store when the cashier sticks his head out the window and shouts, "HEY! Got some time? Want a little cash?"

He needs help moving cases of compressed pop fizz into the back room. "We go through, like, three of these a week, now," he explains. "People in this town are absolutely fiends for soda. There's three soda jerks in this neighborhood alone and we're still making a killing."

"I can't stand the stuff, though," he admits. "And… I'm not sure it's right." How do you mean? "You ever read the ingredients?" he asks. "Curled my hair. No lie." And with that cryptic warning, he tosses you some coins and gets back to selling soda.

You're sitting near a bus stop when a whole schoolbus full of uniformed tykes disembarks. Their teacher whispers something to them; they line up, and one by one they each drop a small coin in your hat.
The teacher is last in line. She doesn't drop a coin. She does, however, drop a flyer with instructions on how to get to her church. Oh well—you can't argue with this much cash!
No luck. Hard hearts in this town—whether from thrift or scorn, you can't tell. Time to go, probably.

stories.title: Money Major City8
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

You hit four factories, but nobody's hiring today. Soon you notice you're cruising around the city with the same loose group of rejected laborers—coughing men in baggy clothes, women with babies tied to their backs, an older fellow with only one hand.
After the fifth factory, everyone makes a silent agreement to give up. You sit on the curb across from the factory doors and eat your sad little lunches together in silence. Screw this city, huh?
A group of young women comes hurrying down the sidewalk. Late to something, probably—but one takes a moment to stay behind and fish some coins out of her purse for you.

God, she's really struggling with that coin purse—shifting in place, nervously glancing at her watch—and her friends are getting further and further away. Her hand slips; coins scatter across the pavement. "Fuck," she blurts. "Keep it all!"
She doesn't hear your appreciation. She's already hurrying down the street, heels kicking high as she breaks into a run.
You sit on the pavement until your butt hurts, but nobody gives you so much as a penny. Screw this town. It's time to get going.

stories.title: Money Major City9
en: You wander the streets of the city looking for a way to make some cash.

"I'm feelin' good about today," crows a young man in line with you outside this factory. "Feelin' pretty good! Today's our lucky day!" "Shut up, Bill! Every time you say that, nobody's hiring!" shouts a man further back in line.

The doors burst open. "WE'RE TAKIN' ALL COMERS," shouts the floor manager. Bill gives a whoop. "I knew it!" he crows. You cheer along with Bill. "Fuck you, Bill," the cynic shouts. "You had nothin' to do with this!" Whether or not he did, though, you all get paid!

The doors burst open. "WE'RE TAKIN' ALL COMERS," shouts the floor manager. Bill gives a whoop. "I'm lucky!" he crows. You (and everyone else in line) groan and laugh. "You had nothin' to do with this!" the cynic shouts. Whether or not Bill did, though, you all get paid!

You're sitting at the corner of a major shopping street. Under a nearby streetlight, a young man stops his girlfriend and kneels; you catch a glint of light in the box in his hand. The girl shrieks and kisses him. Must be a yes!

The young couple stroll toward you, arm in arm, whispering sweet secrets. When they pass you, the young man bends toward your hat. A shower of bright coins tumble down. "Buy yourself something nice," he exclaims. Ahh, the charity of a lovebird!
No luck. Either nobody in this town has any money to give, or nobody in this town has a drop of charity in their damn heart. Time to go, probably.

stories.title: Mother And Child
en: Lost in your own head, you almost walk straight into this woman in your path. Her expression is imperious; she clasps a large toddler in her arms. He's the one who speaks first. "This is a toll road, stranger," he says, voice thuggish beyond his years. "Thirty cents."
"Look at me," the toddler orders. "Look at me. You're dealing with me." The woman, through her silence, suggests assent.

"Do not walk away!" the child shouts right in your ear as you force your way past. You turn to give the pair a withering look over your shoulder, but just as you look back the mother throws her son at you. He looks real mad.
You swiftly sidestep the child projectile. He hits the ground and shatters. Porcelain fragments skitter over the dusty road. "Raymond, no!" the woman wails. "Not again!"
The child tackles you by the neck and takes you down. He pummels you right in the face for a good long while before you wriggle away. It hurts more than you'd be comfortable to admit.

Dismissively, you toss some coins at the ground. The toddler, wide-eyed, leaps from his mother's arms after his loot. "Raymond, no!" she shrieks. Raymond hits the gravel and shatters, sending porcelain fragments skittering over the road.
ru: Задумавшись, вы чуть не врезаетесь в женщину, оказавшуюся у вас на пути. Взгляд у нее высокомерный, она прижимает к себе крупного ребенка. Он первым открывает рот. «Это платная дорога, — заявляет парень чрезмерно кровожадным для его возраста голосом. — С тебя тридцать центов».
«На меня смотри, — приказывает ребенок. — На меня. Ты со мной дела будешь вести». Взгляд женщины, хоть она и молчит, выражает согласие.

«Не смей уходить!» — орет ребенок практически вам в ухо, когда вы отодвигаете их в сторону. Вы оглядываетесь, окидывая парочку презрительным взглядом, но в этот миг женщина швыряет ребенка прямо в вас. Кажется, он и правда взбешен.
Вы ловко уворачиваетесь от летящего ребенка. Он падает на землю и разбивается. По пыльной дороге рассыпаются осколки фарфора. «Раймонд! — кричит женщина. — Только не снова!»
Ребенок хватает вас за шею и заставляет нагнуться. Прежде чем вам удается вырваться, он успевает несколько раз сильно ударить вас по лицу. Это было куда больнее, чем можно было бы ожидать.

Вы равнодушно швыряете на землю несколько монет. Ребенок возбужденно вырывается из рук матери и бросается к добыче. «Раймонд, стой!» — кричит женщина. Парень спотыкается на гравии и рассыпается фарфоровыми осколками по дороге.

stories.title: Moustache Man
en: Here's a derelict school-building—shutters nailed shut, wind-drifted dunes piled against the walls, broken desks lined up in the basketball court. While you rest on the front porch, the doors open and someone gives a startled yelp.
He's an older man, untidy and unshaven, carrying a toolbox in one hand and brandishing a broom in the other. "Don't squat here," he growls. "We're not abandoned!"
You book it across the baseball diamond. He doesn't follow. And when you reach the road, you look back and see him pacing in the basketball court—teaching to the rows of empty desks.
He gives you a hard look—but relents, and joins you in the shade. "I used to teach here," he says, staring off across the baseball diamond. "Now they just pay me to keep the roof up."
ru: Впереди заброшенное здание школы — окна наглухо заколочены, у стен скопились горы песка, на баскетбольной площадке сложены поломанные парты. Пока вы отдыхаете на крыльце, дверь открывается и раздается испуганный вскрик.
Перед вами пожилой мужчина — неряшливый и небритый — с коробкой инструментов в одной руке и метлой в другой. «Нечего тут рассиживаться, — ворчит он. — Здание не заброшено!»
Вы пересекаете спортивную площадку. Он вас не преследует. Выйдя на дорогу, вы оглядываетесь и видите, как тот человек меряет шагами баскетбольное поле... и что-то объясняет пустым партам.

Он сурово смотрит на вас... но потом успокаивается и присаживается рядом в тени. «Когда-то я преподавал здесь, — произносит он, глядя на баскетбольную площадку. — Теперь мне платят за то, что я охраняю это место».

stories.title: Musicians
en: You come across the two musicians on the corner, playing no louder than a murmur. The blind one on the left doesn't sing so much as moan, "If we are willing, He will teach us/to love our brothers, to dance and sing."
When they notice you're gone, the song sputters to a halt. "Philistine!" one of them shouts, but you've moved on.
It continues: "We dream of His seat in Heaven/Around our heads, His flowers ring."
"O Prince in Heaven, we sing for rapture/We all must perish, our flowers and our names/But the flowers in our Prince's kingdom/They shall not perish; they shall remain."

"There is joy there, and there is friendship/for our passage, we shall sing/We dream of His seat in Heaven/Around our heads, His flowers ring." They stop and look at you expectantly, nodding at their empty hat.
You throw them a coin. "Obliged," they both say, and sing the song all over again.
"Philistine!" one of them calls after you. "Ingrate!" When you don't turn around, they perform the song all over again.
ru: Вы встречаете двух музыкантов, что-то едва слышно наигрывающих на углу. Слепой, что слева, не столько поет, сколько стонет: «Если только захотим, Он научит нас братской любви, танцам и песням».
Поняв, что вы уходите, они прекращают петь. «Филистимлянин!» — выкрикивает один из них в вашу удаляющуюся спину.
Вы слушаете дальше: «Мы грезим о Его небесном престоле, вокруг нас звенят Его цветы».
«Принц наш Небесный, мы славим тебя, пусть даже истлеют наши тела, имена и цветы, но не случится того с цветами Его, они не увянут вовек».
«Пусть радость и дружба в наших песнях звучат. Мы грезим о Его небесном престоле, вокруг нас звенят Его цветы». Певцы умолкают и вопросительно поворачиваются к вам, кивая на пустую шляпу.
Вы бросаете им монету. «Благодарим», — дружно произносят они и вновь затягивают ту же песню.
«Филистимлянин! — кричит один из них. — Позор!» Вы не оборачиваетесь, и они вновь затягивают ту же песню.

stories.title: Mysterious Package
en: Off the road and into the woods, you can't help but come across this package by the old tree, tied to a sturdy stick. The cloth wrapping conceals, though not particularly well, something large and softly unsettled. Little eyes blink back at you from inside the bundle.
The shape gives a start. "Please, don't tell my pa that I'm in here," it says in a small voice.
You turn your back, but the parcel calls out to you in a whisper. "I know you saw me," it says. "Please don't tell my pa that I'm here."
"Pa doesn't want to live with us anymore, but I want to go with him. Don't tell him, please. I'm hiding."
You tell the boy you'll keep his secret. You don't see his father anywhere. You don’t see another soul for miles.

His father must have been here at some point, but you sure can't see him now. "Please go, he's coming back any minute," says the boy, growing agitated. "He's going to see you talking to me! Please go!" He only calms down when you leave. You don't see another soul for miles.
ru: Свернув с дороги в лес, вы не можете не обратить внимание на сверток, привязанный к прочной палке. Ткань, пусть и не слишком хорошо, но скрывает довольно крупный и не особо спокойный объект. На вас смотрят крохотные глазки.
Фигура приходит в движение. «Прошу, не говорите папе, что я здесь», — раздается слабый голосок.
Вы отворачиваетесь, чтобы уйти, но сверток шепотом окликает вас. «Я знаю, что вы меня заметили, — говорит он. — Прошу, не рассказывайте папе, что я здесь».
«Папа не хочет жить с нами, но я отправлюсь с ним. Не рассказывайте ему. Я тут прячусь».
Вы обещаете парню хранить его тайну. Но отца нигде не видно. Вы уже давно никого не встречали.

Возможно, его отец и был здесь, но сейчас его нет. «Уходите! Он может вернуться в любую минуту, — мальчик начинает беспокоиться. — Он заметит, как мы разговариваем! Уходите!» Он успокаивается, только когда вы удаляетесь. Вы несколько миль не встречали ни единой души.

stories.title: New Baby
en: There's a commotion outside the post office. The crowd parts, and a middle-aged man comes leaping out onto the curb. "My daughter had a baby," he shouts. "She had a baby girl!"

In a fit of frantic excitement, he kicks over the post-office box, knocks over a bench, and seizes you at random in a bear-hug. "Somebody call my wife," he shouts over your shoulder. "Tell her we're taking the train to Chicago!"
The man starts to dance. His feet hit the pavement so hard, they throw up puffs of shattered stone. Everyone staggers. When he swings around the lamp-post, the metal bends like soft clay.
You grab the man by the shoulders to shake some sense into him, but he mistakes your gesture for an invitation to dance. He swings you around so hard, you fly across the road and into the ditch.

Everyone in town is running for the hills. As you flee down the road, you see him two-hands-overhead lift a car and hurl it ten yards down an alley. Lordy! If this is what the grandfather can do on a good day, then what must the baby be like?
The new grandfather grabs the nearest car and two-hands-overhead lifts it up and hurls it across the road. "MY DAUGHTER HAD A BABY!" he shouts. Everyone runs indoors.

The new grandfather seizes your hands and whirls you around so fast that you feel the blood leave your tingling face. "I've never been happier in my life," he shouts. But his grip slips; before you can react, you're tumbling across the roof of the hardware store across the road.

The man doesn't seem to have noticed he's lost you—he's spinning so fast you can barely see him. As you climb down into the alley and run for the edge of town, you hear him thanking God for his answered prayers over the sound of cracking bricks.

He's already moved on to someone else. He shakes a man's hand so hard, the poor soul face-plants into the pavement. He whirls a woman around so quickly, she slips from his grip and flies across the road into the ditch. When he swings around the lamp-post, the metal bends like soft clay.

You shout and shake your hands at him, trying to catch his attention, but he mistakes your gesture for an invitation to dance. As he tosses you into the air, you catch glimpses of his footsteps cracking the pavement. "MY DAUGHTER HAD A BABY!" he shouts. Everyone runs indoors.

Eventually, he accidentally slings you into the bushes. As you flee, you see him spinning around so fast the gust of wind from his billowing coat buffets a car across the street. Lordy! If this is what the grandfather can do, what's the baby like?
ru: У почтамта какое-то собрание. Толпа разделяется, и на бордюр запрыгивает мужчина средних лет. «У моей дочери ребенок! — кричит он. — У нее дочка!»

В безумном восторге он переворачивает почтовый ящик, перепрыгивает через скамейку и сжимает вас в медвежьих объятиях. «Кто-нибудь, позвоните моей жене, — кричит он через ваше плечо. — Скажите, что мы едем в Чикаго!»

Мужчина пускается в пляс. Его ноги с такой силой обрушиваются на мощеную дорогу, что выбивают из нее камни. Люди разбегаются. Мужчина начинает кружиться вокруг фонарного столба, и металл сминается, подобно мягкой глине.

Вы хватаете чудака за плечи и пытаетесь привести его в чувство, но он по ошибке принимает это за приглашение на танец. Он раскручивает вас с такой силой, что вы отлетаете на другую сторону дороги и падаете в канаву.

Все жители города бегут к холмам. Унося ноги по дороге, вы видите, как мужчина поднимает над головой чью-то машину и отшвыривает ее ярдов на десять. Господи! Если на такое способен дед, то на что же похож ребенок?
Новоиспеченный дед хватает соседнюю машину, поднимает ту над головой и швыряет через дорогу. «У МОЕЙ ДОЧЕРИ РЕБЕНОК!» — орет он. Все забегают внутрь.

Новоиспеченный дед хватает вас за руки и раскручивает так, что у вас кровь от лица отливает. — «Никогда еще не был так счастлив», — кричит мужчина. Его ладони разжимаются, и вы, не успев ничего предпринять, взлетаете на крышу скобяной лавки через дорогу.

Мужчина словно и не замечает вашего исчезновения... он кружится так быстро, что вы его уже почти и не видите. Спустившись в переулок и устремляясь на другой конец города, вы слышите как он славит Господа за ответ на молитвы и крушит ногами камни.

Он уже нашел себе новую жертву. Новоиспеченный дед с такой силой трясет человеку руку, что бедолага падает на дорогу. Затем радостный мужчина раскручивает женщину, и та отлетает в канаву. Мужчина начинает кружиться вокруг фонарного столба, и металл сминается, подобно мягкой глине.

Вы кричите и трясете чудака за плечи, пытаясь привлечь его внимание, но он по ошибке принимает это за приглашение на танец. Он подбрасывает вас в воздух, и вы видите, как его ноги выбивают камни из мостовой. «У МОЕЙ ДОЧЕРИ РЕБЕНОК!» — орет он. Все забегают внутрь.

Внезапно он забрасывает вас в кусты. Еще в полете вы видите, что «дедуля» крутится с такой скоростью, что поднявшийся ветер сдувает машину. Боженька! Если на такое способен дед, то на что же похож ребенок?

stories.title: New Orleans Antique Store
en: Lenny's Antiques has a heady smell—polish, maybe, or incense. Sunlight doesn't penetrate the blacked-out windows. The place is crammed with furniture and curios. The woman behind the counter beckons you over. "I know the look o' you. Know what you're 'ere for."

She sets a tray on the counter. On it sits a hodgepodge of stitched leather pouches of various shapes and sizes. Some have neck or wrist straps looped through them. She waves a hand across the display. "Good luck charms."
"I don' want your money. You got something better." She licks her lips, and holds out a flat palm.

Her knife is fast. She slices a thin line across your palm, then snatches your hand and squeezes. She catches the welling blood in a murky glass vial. Your vision flickers, and as you blink, the place lightens. Sunlight streams through the windows. You are alone.
As you reach the door, a man calls after you. "Is this yours?" His name badge reads 'Lenny'. He's holding up a leather pouch by its strap. You take it and hurry out of the shop.
Her eyes narrow. "No one comes in here to turn me down." She moves as a whirlwind. She grabs you and pulls you in.
You wake up in the street as the sun dips below the horizon. Your right palm stings—it's smeared with blood from a recent cut. In your other hand you hold one of the pouches.
ru: В «Антиквариате Ленни» стоит пряный запах... должно быть, полировка или благовония. Солнечный свет не проникает сквозь затемненные окна. Вокруг полно старой мебели и диковинок. Вас подзывает расположившаяся за стойкой женщина: «Знакомый взгляд. Я знаю, что ты ищешь».
Она опускает на стойку какой-то поднос. На нем лежат кожаные мешочки различных форм и размеров. Некоторые имеют даже ремешки для запястья или шеи. Женщина проводит рукой: «Талисманы удачи».
«Мне не нужны твои деньги. У тебя есть кое-что получше», — она облизывает губы и протягивает ладонь.

Быстро мелькает нож. Женщина надрезает вашу руку, а затем сжимает ее. Стекающую кровь хозяйка лавки помещает в мутный стеклянный флакон. У вас мерцает в глазах, вы моргаете, и вдруг мир становится ярче. Сквозь окна льются потоки света. Вы остаетесь одни.

Когда вы направляетесь к двери, вас окликает мужской голос: «Это ваше?» На нагрудном значке продавца написано «Ленни». Человек держит за ремешок кожаный мешочек. Вы берете его и торопливо покидаете магазин.
Ее глаза превращаются в щелки. «Никто из зашедших сюда не смеет мне отказывать», — женщина движется быстрее ветра. Она хватает вас и притягивает.
Вы приходите в себя на улице. Солнце уже опускается за горизонт. Ваша правая ладонь болит... на ней видны недавний порез и кровь. В другой руке вы сжимаете один из мешочков.

stories.title: Nightshade
en: You find her at a crossroads in the dark, lit by a tiny brazier burning something fragrant and smoky; all around are the dried stems and petals of a dozen strange plants. "You." Her voice is powerful, belying her size. "You seem like you could do with powerful magic."
"For you? No charge. We have a friend in common." She taps her nose knowingly. "You've the look about you of someone who desperately wants something. Just tell me: Endless wealth? Undying love?"

"How practical! How clever." She sprinkles powders and grains into the burning coals, filling the smoke with strange and acrid smells. Soon you're coughing forcefully, feeling something coming up from deep in your throat.
Her eyes, red like coals, stare right into yours as you spit it out. At first you think it's blood—but no; the copper you taste is a single, lonely penny.
"Off with you! Your only wealth is in tales, your only riches are verses." Her laugh is too sharp, bird-like. And with a flick of the wrist, she snuffs out her brazier.

"Deadly nightshade, for bottomless devotion. Asafoetida, for relentless lust. Hellebore, for overwhelming need…" You're wreathed in a cloud of smoke, causing your eyes to water and your nostrils to burn. Though you can barely see, you can tell she has her eyes on yours.
"Off with you! Your only love is the road, your only lust is for trail-dust." Her laugh is too sharp, bird-like. And with a flick of the wrist, she snuffs out her brazier.
"How curious! The magic won't cling to you; it slides off your shade like water off a duck." Did she always know this would happen?
ru: Вы встречаете ее на темном перекрестке, освещенном лишь крохотной жаровней, в которой тлеет нечто дымное и ароматное; вокруг видны сухие стебли десятков видов странных растений. «Эй, ты, — какой удивительно мощный для ее размеров голос. — Похоже, ты сумеешь управиться с могущественной магией».
«Тебе? Бесплатно. У нас есть общий друг, — она с мудрым видом потирает переносицу. — Ты выглядишь так, будто отчаянно что-то ищешь. Просто ответь... Бесконечное богатство? Вечную любовь?»

«Как практично. И умно»,— она сыпет какие-то зерна и порошки на тлеющие угли, придавая дыму странный едкий аромат. Вскоре вы заходитесь кашлем. Возникает чувство, будто что-то стремится выбраться из вашего горла.
Вас сверлят взором красные, точно угли, глаза, пока вы извергаете это из себя. Вначале вам кажется, что это кровь... но, нет. Медный привкус слюне давала одинокая монетка.
«Ступай прочь! Твое богатство лишь в сказаниях, а драгоценности найдешь в стихах», — она заходится каркающим смехом. Она взмахивает рукой, и жаровня гаснет.

«Гибельный паслен для бездонной привязанности. Асафетида для неутолимой страсти. Чемерица для пожирающей нужды...» — вас охватывает облако дыма, заставляющего слезиться глаза и обжигающего ноздри. Вы почти ничего не видите, но понимаете, что она смотрит на вас.
«Ступай прочь! Твоя любовь в странствиях, а страсть — дорожная пыль», — она заходится каркающим смехом. Она взмахивает рукой, и жаровня гаснет.
«Любопытно! Магия не цепляется к тебе; она стекает с твоей тени, точно с гуся вода». Знала ли она, что так и будет?

stories.title: Not Drunk
en: The man squints at you, a smile spreading on his face. You feel exposed, like he's picturing you naked. "I can see your light," he slurs.
He snorts, possibly in mirth. "No." He taps his nose and drops to a stage whisper. "It runs deeper." He offers you the bag. "You can see, too."
"It's an Ee-licks-ear." He opens his mouth wide to shape each syllable. "There are these byoootiful little berries. They let you see the light."
"But everybody gotta have the chance to see." He chuckles for a few seconds longer than is comfortable. "It's like you're a part of errything, and errything's a part of you."
He catches sight of a butterfly and instantly loses interest in you. "So much light in the world."
It's bitter, but warmth rushes through you as it slides down your throat. Your eyes start to tingle. There's something behind him, a glow creeping over his shoulder.
Your vision swims. You can see the light of every living thing, coruscating colors, patterned auras clinging to everything.
Light bleeds into light; everything feels connected. You have a sense of one-ness, a feeling of inner har—
The butterfly's wreathed in green, trailing red smoke. It's the most beautiful thing you have ever seen. You must chase it immediately.
You follow for what feels like a few minutes, but as the sight fades and the stomach cramps start, you realize hours have passed.
Your eyeballs ache and you feel exhausted, but the warmth stays within you. You could see so much light in the world.
ru: По лицу мужчины растекается улыбка, и он подмигивает вам. Этот человек словно раздевает вас взглядом. «Я вижу твой свет», — бормочет он.
Он весело шмыгает носом. «Нет, — — он постукивает себя по носу и издает театральный вздох. — Все куда глубже». Он протягивает вам мешок: «Ты тоже это можешь увидеть».
«Это еле-иик-сир, — он широко раскрывает рот, растягивая каждый звук. — Эти пыыыркрасные ягодки... Они помогают узреть свет».
«У каждого должен быть шанс увидеть, — он так долго смеется, что вам становится неуютно. — Это часть всееего, включая и тьбя!»
Он замечает бабочку и тут же теряет к вам интерес: «Как много света в этом мире».
По вашему горлу прокатывается волна горьковатого тепла. Глаза начинает пощипывать. Вы видите какое-то мерцание за его плечами.
Зрение расплывается. Вы видите свет каждого живого существа; мир наполняется яркими красками переплетающихся ореолов.
Все источает свет, все кажется взаимосвязанным. Вы ощущаете единение с миром, внутреннюю гармо...
Мимо пролетает бабочка, окутанная зеленым сиянием и оставляющая за собой красную дымку. Ничего прекраснее вы не видели. Ее надо срочно догнать!
Казалось, что вы бежали всего пару минут, но, когда ноги начинают вас подводить, а желудок скручивает от голода, становится ясно, что прошло несколько часов.
Ваши глаза пылают, вы устали, но все еще ощущаете внутреннее тепло. Как много света в этом мире.

stories.title: Oil Woman
en: "That one's got a wild spirit to her," she remarks, sweat pooling under her dark brown eyes. The car, halted in the middle of her garage, is a groaning, hulking beast; a gorgeous pre-Ford monstrosity, handmade for speed and grace and perhaps not so much durability.
"A ghost, a wight, a soul, whatever you wanna call it. Of course cars have 'em." She sighs. "But every year there's less wild ones and more of those damn model Bs, tame things, weak and sorry."

She strokes the swooping hood of the luxury car like one might groom a prize stallion. "These beauties… not even their owners really understand them. But today's cars have petty souls. They're meant to ferry accountants to and fro, not to run wild on the open road."
"It is, and it should be!", she cackles. "Gods save me from the mealy-mouthed whining of weak engines. Any fool can drive a Ford—and so, every fool will."

"Oh, but it can. They might not make them like we used to, but we can make the new ones better. Kindle the fires of the deadened soul of the modern car." She points towards a motley pile of steel and chrome on the corner of her shop, pieces salvaged from all kinds of machines.
"We can give them bigger engines, bigger wheels, bigger power. If men have given up on building monsters, who's to say this woman can't turn their pets into monsters?"
ru: «У нее дикий норов», — замечает она. По ее скулам под темно-карими глазами катится пот. Машина, стоящая посреди ее гаража, — настоящее чудище, огромное и громогласное; великолепный зверь дофордовой эпохи, собранный вручную. Она быстра и изящна, хотя и не слишком безопасна.

«Норов, характер, душа — называй как хочешь. У машин это определенно есть, — она вздыхает. — Но с каждым годом становится все меньше диких и больше проклятых прирученных моделей «B» — слабовольных и унылых».

Она потирает хищный изгиб корпуса машины так, как наездник гладит элитного скакуна: «Прекрасные создания... но даже владельцы не всегда этого понимают. Современные машины слабы душой. Только и умеют катать людей туда-сюда, но не вольны бежать по открытой дороге».
«Это так, и мне нравится! — смеется она. — Упаси меня боги от трусливо скулящих маломощных движков. Любой дурак может оседлать «форд»... и поэтому захочет этого».

«О, но это возможно. Пусть они и перестали собирать их в привычном нам формате, но мы можем сделать новые лучше. Разжечь огонь в усмиренной душе современной машины», — она показывает на сверкающую сталью и хромом груду деталей, снятых с разных машин и сваленных в углу гаража.
«Мы можем подарить им мощные движки, большие колеса и силу. Если мужчины стали бояться создавать чудовищ, то почему бы женщинам не начать превращать в чудовищ своих ручных питомцев?»

stories.title: Pair Of Men
en: Two brothers stroll up to you in the street, wearing identical scowls and identical steel-toed boots. One spits in front of you. "Don't stay in town tonight," the other says. "No vagrants after dark."
You hide under a pile of wooden pallets behind the bus station. Round midnight, you see silhouettes searching through the alleys nearby—but they don't find you.
You hide in an alley, but around midnight you're woken by bright lights and a rain of boots. As they hurl you back onto the road, you catch two familiar faces in the crowd—this time, smiling.
There's no shelter to find on the road, and the night is cold and windy. You doze fitfully under a bush, but at least you're in one piece come morning.
ru: К вам по улице направляются два брата с одинаково хмурыми лицами и в одинаковых сапогах со стальными мысами. Один плюет вам под ноги. «Чтобы к вечеру тебя в городе не было, — говорит второй. — Никаких бродяг после заката».
Вы находите убежище под грудой дощатых поддонов позади автобусной остановки. Ближе к полуночи вы замечаете, как по проулкам рыскают чьи-то тени... но вас не находят.
Вы прячетесь в проулке, но ближе к полуночи вас будит яркий свет и град ударов сапогами. Когда вас вышвыривают на дорогу, в толпе вы замечаете пару уже знакомых лиц, но в этот раз они улыбаются.
На дороге пристанища не найти, а ночь холодна и наполнена ветром. Вы с трудом устраиваетесь под кустом, но хотя бы в безопасности встречаете рассвет.

stories.title: Peddler
en: This dapper little peddler shifts restlessly from foot to foot beside his cart, wringing his hands and glancing around as if he's in some kind of mild agony. "Hey," he calls, holding up a quarter. "I've gotta piss. Will you watch my stuff for a minute?"

He flips you a quarter, then hurries off down the road. Five minutes later, he still hasn't returned—but a whole crowd is marching toward you from the other direction. They start shoving and screaming at you.
A man grabs you by the arm. "You working with him?" He shows you six tiny, bloody teeth in the palm of his hand. "My daughter's dying!"

You show them the quarter and point them off down the road, and—thank goodness—they believe you. Most rush off after the peddler, but five or six stay behind to kick the cart over and stomp everything to pieces.
No matter how you protest, they refuse to believe you weren't involved in the scam. Two drag you off to the side of the road and begin to work you over with a bunch of rocks in the end of a sock.

But someone puts a flame to the peddler's cart—it suddenly explodes in a shower of foul-smelling cures. Your assailants bolt, leaving you face-down in the mud, burning scraps of who-knows-what raining down all around you. Fuck—but at least your teeth are still in!
ru: Опрятно одетый торговец нетерпеливо переминается с ноги на ногу у своей тележки, сжимая кулаки и оглядываясь по сторонам так, словно его мучает жуткая боль. «Эй! — подзывает он, показывая четвертак. — Мне надо справить нужду. Приглядишь минутку за моим товаром?»
Он кидает вам монету и торопливо убегает по дороге. Проходит пять минут, но его так и не видно... зато с противоположной стороны к вам направляется толпа. Люди начинают орать и толкать вас.
Какой-то мужчина хватает вас за плечо: «Ты с ним заодно?» Он демонстрирует вам ладонь, в которой лежат шесть крохотных окровавленных зубов: «Моя дочь умирает!»

Вы демонстрируете им четвертак и указываете направление... к счастью, вам верят. Основная масса людей устремляется вслед за торговцем, но человек пять или шесть опрокидывают тележку и начинают крушить товар.
Что бы вы ни говорили, в вашу непричастность верить отказываются. Двое оттаскивают вас на обочину и начинают избивать камнями, набитыми в носок.

Но тут кто-то поджигает тележку торговца... и она вдруг взрывается. Во все стороны разлетаются брызги вонючего зелья. Мучители разбегаются, оставляя вас валяться под дождем грязных, обжигающих остатков непонятного вещества. Проклятье... ну хоть бы зубы на месте!

stories.title: Photography
en: "Want your picture taken?" The man's smile is eager; his teeth are sharp. His companion glances up sharply. "I told you. I don't like it. No more till we know it's safe."

The second man spits his words out. "We're killing people. We take their damn picture—a few weeks later a newspaper wants it. And it's always for a fucking obituary." The sharp-toothed man shrugs. "Traveling alone is dangerous. Not our fault. So, want a photograph?"
"Back a bit. Back a... there!" The sharp-toothed man fusses over the camera, ignoring his scowling companion. "Now just hold it. Hold it... perfect. Wait an hour, and I'll have it ready."

When the men come out of the darkroom, their moods are reversed. That eager sharp-toothed man is working his jaw furiously, as if chewing on bad tobacco. His friend beams as he calls to you. "Terrible picture. You're just a blur. No idea why, but I reckon it can't harm you."

Neither responds immediately. The sullen man barks a laugh. "Not so sure now, are you? It's your damn camera. But fuck it—I'm no coward. You get in the photograph, so will I." His goad works. His sharp-toothed companion jerks his chin up and strides in front of the lens.

The men rush to their darkroom. They are out barely twenty minutes later. Neither looks happy. The sharp-toothed man thrusts the picture at you. "Doesn't make sense—must be broken." His image is sharp, in perfect focus. His companion appears as only a blur.
ru: «Не хочешь сфотографироваться?» — на лице мужчины широкая улыбка, демонстрирующая острые зубы. Его напарник нервно оглядывается: «Я уже говорил. Не нравится мне это. Надо убедиться, что мы в безопасности».

Второй мужчина просто выплевывает слова: «Мы убиваем людей. Делаем чертовы снимки... и спустя пару недель ими интересуется газета. И всегда для очередного треклятого некролога». Острозубый пожимает плечами: «В одиночку бродить опасно. Не наша в том вина. Так желаешь сфотографироваться?»
«Чуть назад. Еще... вот! — острозубый возится с камерой, не обращая внимания на хмурый взгляд напарника. — Не двигаемся... Стоим... Отлично. Обожди часок — и будет готово».

Когда мужчины выходят из проявочной, настроение у них сильно различается. Прежде веселый острозубый мужчина яростно двигает челюстью, словно жует табак. Его же приятель улыбается и подзывает вас: «Ужасный снимок. Все размыто. Не знаю, почему так, но зато и тебе повредить не должно».

Они отвечают не сразу. Грустный мужчина разражается смехом: «Теперь не столь уверен, а? Это все твоя чертова камера. Но, плевать... Я не трус. Раз так хочешь, снимемся вместе». Подначка сработала. Острозубый фотограф чешет подбородок и встает перед объективом.

Мужчины скрываются в проявочной. Выходят они оттуда едва ли спустя двадцать минут. Ни один не улыбается. Острозубый швыряет вам снимок: «Чушь какая-то... похоже, сломалась». Его снимок отчетлив и идеально сфокусирован. А вот изображение напарника выглядит сплошным пятном.

stories.title: Pig Farmers
en: A family of nine invites you into their home for a meal. Hogs roam free in the yard. They wallow in shady patches of cool mud, not paying any mind as you pass.

During supper the hard wind puts an awful burden on the walls. The glass dishes rumble on the table, but the mother seems calm. "Can't butcher a hog in these parts without memaw hollerin' for pigs feet."
The mother's heavy sigh gives you the impression her children ask this often. "If memaw wants more pigs feet, Heaven can provide."
The mother raises up her shoulders into a stern posture. "I teach my children to only fear the Lord. We don't have haints. Just memaw."
ru: Семья из девяти человек приглашает вас в дом разделить с ними трапезу. Во дворе свободно разгуливают свиньи. Они купаются в лужах холодной грязи, не обращая на вас внимания.

Во время трапезы на стены дома обрушивается порыв шквального ветра. Стеклянные тарелки на столе начинают звенеть, но хозяйка выглядит спокойно. «Бабка всякий раз воет, как мы забиваем свинью. Ноги ей нужны, видите ли, —
хозяйка тяжко вздыхает, словно ей часто приходится говорить это детям. — Если бабка так хочет свиных ног, пусть у Небес просит».
Хозяйка принимает решительную позу: «Я учу детей бояться лишь одного Бога. Нет у нас никаких призраков. Только бабка».

stories.title: Pigeons
en: He leans against a fence and turns to face you as you pass him by. At his back is a bag full of birdseed; he assures you that the gawky birds perching on his body are the last remaining passenger pigeons.

"They look extinct to you?" You're not sure those dull grey pigeons look anything like the pictures you've seen of passenger pigeons, though you can't help thinking they stare at you a little too intently. "Say, you like birds?"

"They're lovely creatures. Guileless, really. Hunted damn near to extinction, weren't you…" He strokes one of his birds under the chin. You think you see drips of blood flecking the creature's dirty grey head.

"I've met lots of people who didn't." He stares at you, and so do the birds. "Shame about what happened to them." One of his birds coos, and you swear there are tiny teeth lining the inside of its beak.
You sense it's about time you start moving on. "You be kind to the little birds now, y'hear!" You hurry along the road, though the flapping of ungainly wings seems to follow you for hours.
ru: Когда вы проходите мимо, он облокачивается на изгородь и поворачивается к вам. В его мешке полно птичьего корма. Мужчина уверяет вас, что сидящие на нем неуклюжие птицы — последние странствующие голуби на свете.

«Неужели они вымрут?» — Эти тускло-серые птицы не слишком похожи на тех странствующих голубей, которых вы видели на картинках, но сейчас важнее то, что они определенно излишне внимательно смотрят на вас. — «Скажи, ты любишь птиц?»
«Очаровательные создания. Такие доверчивые... Вас, бедняжки, почти всех истребили...» — мужчина чешет одну из птиц под клювом. Кажется, вы замечаете капельки крови на грязно-серой голове голубя.

«Я не раз встречал людей, которые их не любят, — он, как и птицы, внимательно смотрит на вас. — Просто позор, что такое произошло». Один из голубей подает голос, и вы готовы поклясться, что увидели в его клюве ряд крохотных зубов.
Вы осознаете, что лучше бы двигаться дальше. — «Не обижай невинных птичек, слышишь меня?!» — Вы устремляетесь прочь, но еще несколько часов продолжает казаться, будто вас преследует хлопанье крыльев.

stories.title: Police Radio
en: The policeman mines you for news from anywhere but here as his radio burbles. You catch a snippet—"Armed robbery in progress at"—before he turns it down.
He waves a hand. "It's just Willie. Every month, after his paycheck goes in, he marches into the bank with his .45 and demands cash. Candice gives it to him, then deducts it from his account later.

"What, do I send him up to county? Fine thing that'd be. Truth is, Willie just ain't very good at using banks, and that's no crime." Gunshots sound a few blocks away. His eyes widen. He kicks the car into gear and roars off, shouting into his radio.

"Right you are. No harm in it. Truth is, Willie just ain't very good at using banks, and that's no crime." Gunshots sound a few blocks away. His eyes widen. He kicks the car into gear and roars off, shouting into his radio.

You get to the bank several minutes later. There's a crowd gathered round the entrance, blocking your view, but the action's over. A woman turns to you. "Someone came in waving a shotgun. Willie was there, put him down, but… poor Willie."
ru: Рация полицейского оживает как раз в тот миг, когда тот приказывает вам собирать слухи в другом месте. Вы ловите обрывок фразы «вооруженное ограбление на...», но тут коп выключает устройство.
Он взмахивает рукой: «Это просто Уилли. Каждый месяц, как получка заканчивается, хватает свой 45-й калибр и отправляется в банк за деньгами. Кэндис отдает ему их, а затем вычитает с его счета».

«И что, посадить его под арест? Можно, конечно. По правде, Уилли просто не умеет пользоваться банком, и это вряд ли преступление». В паре кварталов от вас раздается пальба. Его глаза широко распахиваются. Он прыгает в машину и уносится прочь, крича что-то в рацию.

«Все верно. Никакого вреда. По правде, Уилли просто не умеет пользоваться банком, и это вряд ли преступление». В паре кварталов от вас раздается пальба. Его глаза широко распахиваются. Он прыгает в машину и уносится прочь, крича что-то в рацию.

До банка вы добираетесь несколькими минутами позднее. Толпа у входа загораживает обзор, но все уже кончено. К вам поворачивается женщина: «Кто-то забежал туда, размахивая ружьем. Уилли тоже был там и уложил его, но... бедняга Уилли».

stories.title: Policeman
en: They've taken over a booth at the roadside diner, table strewn with papers and forms. He's in shirtsleeves, revolver hanging loosely off his chest; she's in a moss-green dress from two seasons ago, and a felt hat that's begun to warp.
